To become Kenya's leading digital platform for discovering, planning, and booking authentic travel, cultural, entertainment, and lifestyle experiences beyond traditional wildlife safaris.
To connect tourists, local travelers, event organizers, and tourism businesses through a centralized platform that makes discovering and booking Kenyan experiences simple, secure, and personalized.

Beyond Safari is a web-based tourism discovery and booking platform designed to transform how people explore Kenya. Although Kenya is globally recognized for wildlife tourism, much of its rich cultural, entertainment, culinary, historical, and adventure tourism remains difficult to discover due to fragmented information sources.

The platform will provide a centralized ecosystem where users can discover experiences, compare options, book activities, make secure payments, receive AI-powered recommendations, and interact with an intelligent travel assistant.
The system will initially focus on Kenya and later expand to East Africa and the wider African market.
Kenya attracts millions of visitors annually due to its wildlife attractions, national parks, and coastal tourism. However, tourism information remains fragmented and difficult to access.
As a result, travelers often miss opportunities that match their interests and budgets.
Tourism information exists across multiple disconnected platforms.
Small tourism operators struggle to market their services.
Users often need to switch between several websites and communication channels.
Current platforms rarely provide intelligent recommendations tailored to user preferences.
Users may struggle to verify service providers before making payments.
Develop a centralized platform for discovering and booking authentic Kenyan tourism experiences.
Increase visibility of local tourism experiences.
Enhance user experience through AI recommendations.
Support tourism SMEs through digital exposure.
Create a scalable platform for future African expansion.

The system follows a three-tier architecture, implemented in a serverless model on Firebase rather than a traditional always-on application server:
Firebase Cloud Functions (Node.js/TypeScript) and Firebase Authentication
Cloud Firestore (NoSQL) and Cloud Storage for Firebase
Authorization (Firebase custom claims for role-based access: tourist, business owner, admin)
Reservation processing for experiences, flights, hotels, and cabs (a single booking type field distinguishes the four, since they share the same status/payment lifecycle)
Standalone bookings (e.g. a local user requesting a cab without an associated trip)
Itinerary creation and editing (road trips and multi-day trip plans)
Grouping related bookings under a single trip
Awarding points and badges (e.g. visiting all waterfalls in a county)

As Cloud Firestore is a NoSQL document database rather than a relational one, this section presents the design at two levels: the conceptual entities (technology-agnostic, shown in the ER Diagram in Chapter 25) and the top-level Firestore collections each entity maps to (the physical implementation actually used in development).
users (role field distinguishes tourist, local traveler, business owner, and admin – no separate Roles collection needed)
experiences (covers every bookable or visitable place – waterfalls, parks, nightlife venues, restaurants, theatres – distinguished by a category field rather than separate collections)
categories (reference data: waterfalls, parks, nightlife, food, entertainment, road trips, etc.)
locations (counties/regions reference data; precise coordinates are stored directly on each experience as a GeoPoint)
events (time-scheduled happenings – concerts, movie nights, game nights, theatre performances, night-sky observation – each referencing the experience/venue where it takes place)
trips (user-created itineraries and road trip plans; stores an array of experience references as stops)
bookings (type field: experience, flight, hotel, or cab; tripId is optional so a booking can stand alone, e.g. a local user booking just a cab to a waterfall)
visits (gamification check-in log: links a user, an experience, and a timestamp; badge eligibility is calculated by querying this collection)
badges (badge definitions and unlock criteria, e.g. “visited all waterfalls in Nyeri County”)
Document IDs: each document is identified by an auto-generated Firestore ID, serving the same role as a primary key.

References: fields such as userId, experienceId, and tripId store the ID of the related document, serving the same role as a foreign key. Firestore does not enforce referential integrity automatically, so this is validated in Cloud Functions before writes.
Composite Indexes: defined for compound queries (e.g. filtering experiences by category and county, or visits by user and experience category for badge calculation).
Denormalization: small, rarely-changing fields (e.g. a business’s display name on its experiences) are duplicated onto related documents to avoid extra reads, since Firestore has no join operation.

Security Rules: Firestore Security Rules govern read/write access per collection (e.g. a user may only write to their own user document and bookings; only verified business owners may write to their own business’s experiences), replacing the role of database-level grants in a relational system.

Beyond Safari addresses the fragmentation of tourism information in Kenya by providing a centralized platform that supports experience discovery, booking, payment processing, and personalized recommendations. The platform benefits tourists, local travelers, businesses, and government stakeholders while creating a scalable foundation for future expansion across Africa.
